chunks: A number of our companions, from Aḥmad ibn Muḥammad, from ʿAbd al-Raḥmān ibn Ḥammād and another, from Ḥanān ibn Sadīr al-Ṣayrafī, who said:

I heard Abū ʿAbdillāh (عليه السلام) saying: The Prophet's (صلى الله عليه وآله) own soul was announced to him, while he was sound and had no pain. He said: The Trustworthy Spirit descended with it. He said: So he (صلى الله عليه وآله) called for the salat (prayer) to gather the people, and ordered the Muhājirīn and the Anṣār to come with weapons, and the people assembled.

Then the Prophet (صلى الله عليه وآله) ascended the pulpit and announced his own death to them. Then he said: I adjure by Allah the ruler over my community after me: that he be merciful to the body of the Muslims, honor their elder, show mercy to their weak, and respect their scholar; that he not harm them so as to humiliate them, nor impoverish them so as to lead them to disbelief, nor close his door to them so that their strong would consume their weak, and that he not keep them away in their military expeditions so that the progeny of my community would be cut off.

Then he said: I have conveyed and sincerely advised, so bear witness. And Abū ʿAbdillāh (عليه السلام) said: This was the last speech that the Messenger of Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله) spoke upon his pulpit.

key_terms.الرُّوحُ الْأَمِينُ: The Trustworthy Spirit, referring to Jibrīl conveying the divine message.
key_terms.الصَّلَاةَ جَامِعَةً: A call for the people to gather collectively for an important public assembly.
key_terms.الْأَنْصَارَ: The Helpers of Madinah who supported the Prophet (صلى الله عليه وآله).
key_terms.الْمُهَاجِرِينَ: The Emigrants among the early Muslims.
key_terms.الْوَالِيَ: The ruler or authority over the Muslim community after the Prophet (صلى الله عليه وآله).
key_terms.وَقَّرَ عَالِمَهُمْ: That he should honor and show due respect to their scholar.

ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet (صلى الله عليه وآله) command the ruler after him concerning the rights of the Muslims?
ai.summary: This hadith narrates that the Prophet (صلى الله عليه وآله) was informed of his approaching death while still physically well, after which he gathered the Muslims and addressed them from the pulpit. In his final public counsel, he emphasized the duties of the ruler toward the community: mercy, honoring elders, respecting scholars, avoiding oppression and impoverishment, maintaining access to leadership, and protecting the welfare and continuity of the Ummah.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Abdul Rahman Bin Hammad, and someone else, from Hannan Bin Sadeyr Al Sayrafi who said,

‘I heard Abu Abdullahasws saying: ‘The news of death was given to the Prophetsaww himselfsaww and hesaww was healthy, there wasn’t any pain with himsaww. The Trustworthy Ruh descended with it. So hesaww called for the congregational Salat and ordered the Emigrants and the Helpers with the weapons (to be ready). And the people gathered.

So the Prophet<sup>saww</sup> ascended the Pulpit, and gave the news of death to them himself<sup>saww</sup>, then said: ‘I<sup>saww</sup> remind and caution of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> the ruler from after me<sup>saww</sup> upon my<sup>saww</sup> community, that he should be merciful upon the group of Muslims, honour their elders and be merciful to their young ones, and dignify their scholars, and do not harm them so he would humiliate them, and not to impoverish them so they would disbelieve, and not close his door from them so their strong ones would devour their weak ones, and not pain them in their campaigns, so the lineages of my<sup>saww</sup> community would be cut off’.

Then he<sup>saww</sup> said: ‘I<sup>saww</sup> have delivered and advised, therefore, bear witness!’ And Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘This is the last speech Rasool-Allah<sup>saww</sup> spoke with upon his<sup>saww</sup> Pulpit’.
